title: Syllogistic Translations: Easy
description: Translate everyday English — all, no, some — into syllogistic logic without losing the structure of the claim.

title: Syllogistic Translations: Hard
description: Tackle the trickier idioms — only, every, and sentences that reorder subject and predicate.

title: Propositional Translations: Easy
description: Translate ordinary language into symbols — and, or, if-then — without losing the structure of the argument.

title: Propositional Translations: Hard
description: Handle the connectives that trip people up — unless, only if, and necessary versus sufficient conditions.

title: Modal Translations: Basic
description: Translate claims about what is necessary, possible, and contingent into the box and diamond of modal logic.

title: Modal Translations: Quantified
description: Mix modality with quantifiers, where the order of box, diamond, and “all” changes what a claim says.

title: Deontic Translations: Imperative
description: Translate commands and requests into imperative logic, underlining what is to be done.

title: Deontic Translations: Deontic
description: Translate ought, permissible, and forbidden into deontic logic.

title: Belief Translations: Believing
description: Translate claims about believing, not believing, and withholding belief into belief logic.

title: Belief Translations: Willing
description: Translate wanting, resolving, and acting — the willing side of belief logic — into formulas.

title: Belief Translations: Rationality
description: Translate what is evident, reasonable, and rational to believe into belief-logic formulas.

title: Meanings and Definitions
description: Spot what is wrong with a definition — too broad, too narrow, circular, or worse.

title: Informal Fallacies
description: Read a short passage and name the fallacy it commits — from ad hominem to post hoc.
